key_insight: There is a trade-off between compression and long-horizon forecast reliability: nonlinear autoencoders compress wake data better, but POD produces smoother latent dynamics that are easier to predict and more stable over time.
engineering_relevance: For real-time active flow control, the most compact latent representation is not always the best choice; stability of the reduced dynamics can matter more than maximum reconstruction fidelity.
method: Compared POD with convolutional autoencoders and two variational autoencoders for spatial compression.
Used LSTM-based temporal predictors to forecast latent dynamics.
Tested on two actuated 2D wake flows: a simplified truck wake and the fluidic pinball.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that CAEs give sharper short-term reconstructions, but their latent trajectories are more irregular, with faster long-horizon degradation and a higher chance of catastrophic divergence than POD-based ROMs.
watch_item: Highly compressed nonlinear latent spaces may be harder to extrapolate robustly, so controller design should check long-horizon stability—not just reconstruction error.
paper_title: The balance between compactness and forecast accuracy of data-driven latent-space reduced-order models in controlled wake flows
